tip: 'Doa restu' = 'prayers and blessing' – a fixed wedding-invitation phrase.
Invitation closer: 'atas kehadiran ... terima kasih' – thanks given before the event happens.
'Mohon kehadiran' = 'we request your presence' – spoken this is just 'datang ya'.
'Turut mengundang' = 'also inviting' – the line listing extra hosts at the bottom of invitations.
'Bagi' = formal 'untuk' (for) – invitation and news word; spoken: 'untuk keluarga kami'.
'Kerja bakti' = 'community work day' – a fixed term on neighborhood invitations.
'Pertemuan' = formal 'meeting', from 'bertemu' – schools write 'pertemuan', parents say 'rapat'.
'Termasuk' is literally 'entered (into the group)' – 'masuk' with 'ter-'. 'Termasuk anak-anak' means the children are counted in: 'including'.
'Besar harapan kami' = 'it is our great hope' – a super-polite invitation formula.
'Menantikan' = 'to look forward to, await' – the formal 'menunggu', common in invitations.
'Nasabah' = 'bank customer' – banks use it; shops say 'pelanggan' or 'pembeli'.
'Sebesar' = 'in the amount of' ('se-' + 'besar') – money notices put it before figures.
'Sedang dalam perbaikan' = 'under repair', notice formula – spoken: 'lagi diperbaiki'.
'Kata sandi' = official 'password' – most Indonesians just say 'password'; 'sandi' = code.
'Layanan' = formal 'service', from 'melayani' – in speech, customer service is just 'CS' (ce-es).
'Karyawan' = 'employee', the office word – casual speech says 'pegawai' or 'orang kantor'.
'Diwajibkan' = 'are required to', HR passive – spoken: 'semua harus ikut'.
'Tertelan' = 'accidentally swallowed' – 'ter-' often marks accidents: 'kartunya tertelan mesin'.
'Penarikan uang' = 'withdrawal', bank language – spoken: 'mau ambil uang'.
'Diperbarui' = 'be updated, renewed', from 'baru' (new) – the 'per-' in it means 'make', so: be made new.
'Dihentikan sementara' = 'temporarily suspended', notice-speak – spoken: 'loketnya tutup dulu'.
'Mengalami gangguan' = 'experiencing a disruption', outage-notice formula – spoken: 'lagi error'.
'Atas' after 'terima kasih' = formal 'for': 'terima kasih atas kepercayaan Anda' – speech usually drops 'atas'.
Heard everywhere in speech: 'nggak' = 'tidak'. 'Nggak bisa' = 'tidak bisa' (can't). In writing, use 'tidak'.
'Nggak jadi' = 'ended up not happening': 'jadi' here means 'materialize', so 'nggak jadi pindah' says the move was planned and then fell through.
'Nggak apa-apa' = 'tidak apa-apa' ('it's okay') – one of the most common spoken phrases.
'Udah' = 'sudah' in speech: 'udah makan?' = 'sudah makan?' (eaten yet?)
'Udah berangkat' = 'sudah berangkat' (already left). Spoken form; write 'sudah'.
'Aja' = 'saja' (just): 'di sini aja' = 'di sini saja' (just here).
'Tanya aja' = 'tanya saja' (just ask). 'Aja' follows the word it limits.
